title: Name the Principles You Protect
description: Identify the principles that consistently influence your choices and sense of meaning.
objective: Prioritize personal values using lived evidence.
instructions: Choose ten values from the supplied list or add your own.
Rank your top five, then write one recent decision that showed each value.
prompt: Which values do you want your ordinary week to visibly express?
questions: Which value was easiest to rank?
reflection_prompt: What small choice would better honor your highest value this week?
expected_behavior: Makes decisions with greater awareness of personal priorities.

title: Spot a Values Tension
description: Examine a recent choice where two important principles pulled you in different directions.
objective: Separate competing values from vague indecision.
instructions: Describe the decision without judging the outcome.
Name the two values in tension and design a third option that respects both.
prompt: Where did doing what was right for one priority make another priority harder?
reflection_prompt: How can you make future trade-offs explicit earlier?
expected_behavior: Names trade-offs clearly before committing to difficult choices.

title: Evidence of a Strength
description: Collect specific moments that reveal a capability you can intentionally reuse.
objective: Ground strengths language in observable evidence.
instructions: Recall three moments when you handled something effectively.
For each, record what you did, what capability it required, and who benefited.
prompt: What did you do well recently that you are tempted to dismiss as ordinary?
reflection_prompt: Where could you deliberately use that strength tomorrow?
expected_behavior: Recognizes capabilities using concrete examples rather than labels alone.

title: Strength Under Conditions
description: Discover the environmental conditions that make one of your strengths easier to access.
objective: Link effective performance with supportive conditions.
instructions: Rate your energy, clarity, autonomy, support, and challenge from 1 to 5.
Compare those ratings across two situations where you performed well.
prompt: When do you become the version of yourself that works with unusual ease?
reflection_prompt: What condition can you arrange instead of waiting for it to appear?
expected_behavior: Designs conditions that make effective behavior more likely.

title: Label the Signal
description: Practice identifying an emotion precisely by noticing its thoughts, body cues, and action urge.
objective: Improve precision when naming present emotions.
instructions: Pause and rate the emotion intensity from 1 to 10.
Choose the most precise word available, then note one body sensation and one urge.
prompt: What emotion is present right now, and what is it trying to signal?
reflection_prompt: Did a more precise label change what you needed?
expected_behavior: Names emotional states with more precision before responding.

title: Trigger Chain Map
description: Map the sequence from a triggering event to interpretation, emotion, urge, and action.
objective: Find an earlier point where a response can be chosen.
instructions: Write the observable event without assumptions.
Complete the chain: interpretation, emotion, body cue, urge, action, result.
prompt: What happened immediately before your strongest reaction this week?
reflection_prompt: What alternate interpretation deserves a fair test?
expected_behavior: Notices triggers and separates events from interpretations.

title: Notice the Loop
description: Identify a repeating thought-behavior-outcome loop that is useful or costly.
objective: Make a recurring internal pattern observable.
instructions: Describe three recent examples of the same situation.
Underline the repeated thought and record how it shaped your next action.
prompt: What story appears just before you respond in the same familiar way?
questions: What does the story protect you from?
reflection_prompt: What more balanced story could guide the next iteration?
expected_behavior: Recognizes recurring thoughts as patterns rather than fixed truths.

title: Change the Cue
description: Find a small environmental or temporal cue that reliably starts an unwanted behavior loop.
objective: Interrupt an automatic loop at its earliest cue.
instructions: Choose one repeated behavior and identify its cue and immediate reward.
Write an if-then response that preserves the need through a healthier action.
prompt: When does this behavior usually begin, and what need does it meet?
questions: What replacement is available within two minutes?
reflection_prompt: What did the cue teach you about the underlying need?
expected_behavior: Uses cues as information and introduces a deliberate alternative response.

title: Three Selves Check-In
description: Compare how you see yourself, how others may experience you, and who you are becoming.
objective: Reveal gaps between identity, impact, and intention.
instructions: Write three short descriptions under identity, impact, and aspiration.
Circle one alignment and one gap without turning either into a verdict.
prompt: Where do your intentions and your impact most clearly meet or differ?
questions: What evidence would clarify the gap?
reflection_prompt: What behavior would bring the three descriptions closer together?
expected_behavior: Uses multiple perspectives to refine self-understanding.

title: Weekly Inner Weather Review
description: Review a week of emotional states, choices, and energy to identify useful personal signals.
objective: Turn weekly experience into a practical self-observation habit.
instructions: List three high-energy and three low-energy moments.
For each, note people, setting, activity, emotion, and what you needed.
prompt: What did your week repeatedly try to tell you about your needs?
reflection_prompt: Choose one adjustment for the coming week and define its signal.
expected_behavior: Reviews experience and makes one evidence-informed adjustment.

title: Proof of Progress
description: Build a credible record of past effort, learning, and outcomes to support a current challenge.
objective: Use specific evidence to strengthen self-efficacy.
instructions: List five things you learned or completed despite difficulty.
For each, name the action that made progress possible.
prompt: What past evidence suggests you can learn the next part?
reflection_prompt: How will you use one proven strategy in the current challenge?
expected_behavior: Approaches new tasks with evidence-based self-trust.

title: Transfer the Skill
description: Translate a capability from one successful context into a small experiment in another context.
objective: Test whether a known strength can support a new situation.
instructions: Choose one skill you use reliably and a context where you need more confidence.
Define a ten-minute experiment that uses the same underlying skill.
prompt: What do you already know how to do that resembles this challenge?
questions: What would count as useful evidence?
reflection_prompt: What did the experiment reveal about your capability?
expected_behavior: Uses small experiments to replace global self-doubt with specific evidence.

title: Coach Yourself Through a Mistake
description: Rewrite a harsh inner response as language a wise, honest, supportive coach would use.
objective: Practice constructive self-talk after an imperfect outcome.
instructions: Write the harsh sentence exactly as it appeared.
Answer with three parts: acknowledge the difficulty, name the lesson, choose the next action.
prompt: What would a direct but caring coach say about this mistake?
reflection_prompt: How did compassion preserve accountability rather than remove it?
expected_behavior: Responds to mistakes with learning-focused language and action.

title: Shared Human Difficulty
description: Place a personal struggle in the wider context of learning, uncertainty, and ordinary human limitation.
objective: Reduce isolating shame while preserving useful responsibility.
instructions: Describe the struggle in neutral language.
Write how you would respond if a respected peer described the same experience.
prompt: What part of this difficulty is a normal human experience rather than a personal defect?
questions: What support would you offer that person?
reflection_prompt: Which part of that support can you offer yourself today?
expected_behavior: Maintains perspective and seeks constructive support after difficulty.

title: The Clear Request
description: Turn an unspoken need into a specific, respectful request another person can answer.
objective: Express needs without hinting, blaming, or overexplaining.
instructions: Complete: When [observable situation], I feel/need [impact or need]. Would you [specific request] by [time]?
Say the request aloud once before deciding whether to send it.
prompt: What do you need someone else to know or do that you have not clearly requested?
reflection_prompt: How did specificity change the emotional weight of the request?
expected_behavior: Makes specific requests while respecting the other person’s choice.

title: Boundary With Warmth
description: State a realistic boundary that protects your capacity while keeping the relationship visible.
objective: Practice clear boundaries without apology spirals or aggression.
instructions: Name the limit, the brief reason if useful, and what you can offer instead.
Communicate it to a low-risk person and observe the result.
prompt: Where would a respectful limit make your commitments more sustainable?
questions: What alternative can you genuinely offer?
reflection_prompt: What did you learn about the difference between discomfort and danger?
expected_behavior: Sets and maintains reasonable limits with clear language.

title: One Degree Braver
description: Choose a small, reversible action that moves toward an important goal despite manageable uncertainty.
objective: Build courage through a bounded behavioral experiment.
instructions: Describe the desired direction and the smallest meaningful step.
Set a time, complete the step, and record what actually happened.
prompt: What is one action that is slightly outside your comfort zone but within your control?
reflection_prompt: What did action teach you that thinking could not?
expected_behavior: Takes appropriately sized action before certainty is complete.

title: Act Alongside Doubt
description: Separate the presence of self-doubt from the decision to take a values-aligned next step.
objective: Create a repeatable response when doubt delays action.
instructions: Write the doubt as a prediction, not a fact.
Create an if-then plan: If doubt appears at the start cue, then I will take the first two-minute action.
prompt: What would you do next if doubt could come along without driving?
reflection_prompt: Did confidence need to arrive before action, or follow it?
expected_behavior: Begins valued tasks while acknowledging uncertainty without obeying it.

title: Confidence Calibration
description: Compare a confidence prediction with actual evidence to make future self-assessments more accurate.
objective: Replace vague confidence judgments with calibrated predictions.
instructions: Before a task, predict difficulty, quality, and recovery time from 1 to 10.
Afterward, record actual values and one factor you missed.
prompt: Where is your confidence prediction too pessimistic or too optimistic?
questions: What evidence should influence the next estimate?
reflection_prompt: How can calibration support better choices without becoming self-criticism?
expected_behavior: Makes more specific and evidence-informed judgments about capability.

title: Paraphrase Before Reply
description: Practice confirming another person’s meaning before adding your own view or solution.
objective: Increase accuracy and felt understanding in conversation.
instructions: In one conversation, wait until the speaker finishes.
Say, ‘What I hear is...’ and ask them to correct your summary.
prompt: What would change if understanding came before being understood?
reflection_prompt: How did confirmation affect the quality of the conversation?
expected_behavior: Checks understanding before offering advice or disagreement.

title: The Curious Follow-Up
description: Replace an automatic response with a question that invites the other person’s fuller meaning.
objective: Build listening depth through open, non-leading questions.
instructions: Notice one moment when you want to interrupt or solve.
Ask one open question beginning with what, how, or in what way.
prompt: What question would help you understand the experience beneath the first sentence?
questions: Did the question invite detail or defend a conclusion?
reflection_prompt: What did curiosity make possible?
expected_behavior: Uses open questions to understand rather than steer the speaker.

title: One-Sentence Intent
description: Distill a message to its purpose so the listener can identify what matters quickly.
objective: Make messages easier to understand and act upon.
instructions: Draft your message in five sentences.
Reduce it to one sentence containing context, purpose, and requested next step.
prompt: If the listener remembers only one sentence, what should it be?
questions: What detail is useful but nonessential?
reflection_prompt: What became clearer when you removed explanation?
expected_behavior: Leads with purpose and makes the requested next step visible.

title: Specific Language Swap
description: Replace vague words in a message with observable details, owners, and time boundaries.
objective: Reduce ambiguity that creates avoidable coordination problems.
instructions: Underline words such as soon, better, handle, or some.
Replace each with a concrete action, person, output, or date.
prompt: Which word in this message could mean different things to different readers?
questions: What observable result would remove ambiguity?
reflection_prompt: How did specificity change the recipient’s ability to respond?
expected_behavior: Uses concrete language to make responsibilities and outcomes clear.

title: Observation and Impact
description: Deliver feedback that separates observable behavior from character judgments and labels.
objective: Make feedback specific, respectful, and actionable.
instructions: Write the observable behavior, its impact, and a preferred next step.
Ask whether the person is willing to discuss it before offering the feedback.
prompt: What did you observe, what effect did it have, and what would help next time?
reflection_prompt: Did the message create a path forward rather than a verdict?
expected_behavior: Gives behavior-based feedback with a clear future request.

title: Receive Without Defending
description: Practice listening to feedback long enough to separate useful information from the threat response.
objective: Extract learning from feedback before deciding what to accept.
instructions: Recall recent feedback and write the first defensive thought.
Write three questions that would clarify the example, impact, and desired change.
prompt: What might this feedback be trying to help you see, even if parts are incomplete?
reflection_prompt: How can you receive information without surrendering your judgment?
expected_behavior: Seeks examples and extracts actionable learning before reacting.

title: Repair the Small Rupture
description: Use a short repair attempt after a tense exchange before resentment or avoidance grows.
objective: Restore connection through timely ownership and curiosity.
instructions: Name your part without adding a defense.
Acknowledge impact, ask how it landed, and propose a next step.
prompt: What small tension deserves a repair attempt while it is still workable?
reflection_prompt: What did the other person need to feel heard?
expected_behavior: Initiates respectful repair after contributing to relational tension.

title: Disagree With the Idea
description: Frame a disagreement around evidence, assumptions, and shared outcomes instead of personal worth.
objective: Practice direct disagreement while preserving dignity and collaboration.
instructions: Write the shared goal and the specific point of disagreement.
Use: I see it differently because..., the evidence I am using is..., could we test...?
prompt: How can you challenge the idea without making the person the problem?
questions: What evidence would change your view?
reflection_prompt: What helped keep the disagreement about the work?
expected_behavior: States disagreement directly and remains open to evidence.

title: Conversation Debrief
description: Review one conversation for listening, clarity, emotional tone, and the next relationship move.
objective: Turn everyday conversations into targeted communication practice.
instructions: Rate your listening, clarity, and curiosity from 1 to 5.
Choose one moment and write the response you wish you had tried.
prompt: Where did the conversation become more connected or less clear?
reflection_prompt: What single behavior will you practice in your next conversation?
expected_behavior: Uses communication review to choose one concrete behavior to practice.

title: Protect One Focus Block
description: Design a short period where one meaningful task receives your full available attention.
objective: Create a repeatable environment for focused work.
instructions: Choose a 25-minute task and remove two predictable distractions.
Set a visible start and stop time, then work on one task only.
prompt: What distraction is most predictable, and what boundary would prevent it?
reflection_prompt: What will you keep or change for the next focus block?
expected_behavior: Creates and protects bounded periods of single-task attention.

title: Single-Task Reset
description: Practice returning attention to the chosen task whenever you notice an unrelated pull.
objective: Strengthen attention recovery without self-criticism.
instructions: During one task, place a mark each time attention wanders.
Acknowledge the pull, record it if needed, and return to the next visible action.
prompt: What does your attention keep reaching for instead of the chosen task?
reflection_prompt: What did counting returns reveal about focus practice?
expected_behavior: Returns attention to the selected task more quickly after distraction.

title: The Two-Minute Doorway
description: Reduce the emotional and practical barrier to a delayed task by defining its first tiny action.
objective: Convert avoidance into an immediate, low-friction beginning.
instructions: Write the task and the smallest physical action that starts it.
Do only that action, then decide whether to continue.
prompt: What is the first visible movement, not the whole task?
reflection_prompt: What did the task look like after the first action?
expected_behavior: Begins delayed tasks by identifying and completing a tiny first step.

title: Use a Start Cue
description: Pair a consistent daily cue with a brief starting ritual for one important task.
objective: Make task initiation more automatic and less dependent on mood.
instructions: Choose an existing cue such as coffee, arriving, or closing email.
Write: After [cue], I will [open task and work for ten minutes]. Test it once.
prompt: Which existing routine could reliably open the door to this work?
questions: What exact action follows the cue?
reflection_prompt: Did the cue reduce negotiation with yourself?
expected_behavior: Uses a stable cue to begin priority work with less deliberation.

title: Three Priorities, Not Twelve
description: Choose a realistic daily priority set and make trade-offs visible before the day becomes reactive.
objective: Align daily effort with the most consequential priorities.
instructions: List all candidate tasks, then rank them by consequence and urgency.
Choose three priorities and name what will wait if the day changes.
prompt: What deserves your best attention today, even if everything cannot fit?
questions: What is the cost of deferring each item?
reflection_prompt: Did your calendar match your stated priorities?
expected_behavior: Makes explicit priority trade-offs and protects time for high-value work.

title: Estimate Then Learn
description: Compare expected task duration with actual duration to improve future planning without shame.
objective: Improve time estimates using personal evidence.
instructions: Choose one task and predict its duration before starting.
Record interruptions and actual duration, then identify one source of variance.
prompt: What part of this task is likely to take longer than your first estimate?
questions: What should your next estimate include?
reflection_prompt: How can better estimates make your plans kinder and more accurate?
expected_behavior: Uses observed duration and interruptions to make more realistic plans.

title: Restart Without Drama
description: Practice returning to a task after interruption by choosing the next concrete action.
objective: Shorten the gap between interruption and re-engagement.
instructions: When interrupted, leave a one-line restart note before switching context.
When returning, read it and work for five minutes before evaluating progress.
prompt: What note would make returning obvious to your future self?
reflection_prompt: How much energy did the restart note save?
expected_behavior: Leaves clear restart cues and resumes important tasks after interruptions.

title: Boredom Has a Timer
description: Stay with a meaningful but unexciting task for a defined interval and observe the urge to switch.
objective: Build tolerance for ordinary effort without requiring constant novelty.
instructions: Choose a safe, important task and set a fifteen-minute timer.
Record urges to switch without acting on them until the timer ends.
prompt: What becomes possible when boredom is treated as a passing signal?
reflection_prompt: What helped you continue without forcing exceptional motivation?
expected_behavior: Continues priority work through manageable boredom and returns after setbacks.

title: Friction Audit
description: Inspect a procrastinated task for ambiguity, effort, emotion, or environment that makes starting costly.
objective: Find the real barrier instead of labeling yourself as lazy.
instructions: Rate clarity, effort, emotional discomfort, and environmental friction from 1 to 5.
Choose the highest rating and change one part of the task or setup.
prompt: What exactly is hard about beginning this task?
questions: Which barrier can you change today?
reflection_prompt: What did the audit reveal about the task design?
expected_behavior: Diagnoses and reduces practical barriers before demanding more willpower.

title: Weekly Attention Review
description: Review where attention went, what mattered, and what environmental change would support the next week.
objective: Improve focus systems through weekly observation.
instructions: List two periods of deep work, two common distractions, and one unfinished priority.
Choose one environmental change and schedule its first trial.
prompt: What deserves more protection from your attention next week?
questions: Which distraction was a cue rather than a character flaw?
reflection_prompt: What one system change will you test?
expected_behavior: Adjusts focus systems based on observed attention patterns.

title: Name, Pause, Choose
description: Use a brief pause to recognize an emotional activation and select a response aligned with your goal.
objective: Create choice during emotionally charged moments.
instructions: Name the emotion and rate its intensity.
Take three slow breaths, then choose the response that best serves the situation.
prompt: What response would your goal support after the first emotional wave?
reflection_prompt: Which part of the pause was most useful?
expected_behavior: Pauses and chooses a response instead of acting on the first urge.

title: Response Menu
description: Prepare several constructive responses for a recurring emotional trigger before it happens again.
objective: Increase response flexibility under pressure.
instructions: Name a recurring trigger and list three possible responses: pause, communicate, or exit and return.
Choose the response that fits low, medium, and high intensity.
prompt: What options would you like available before the trigger narrows your attention?
questions: Which response protects both dignity and safety?
reflection_prompt: How does preparation change your sense of choice?
expected_behavior: Uses a prepared response appropriate to the intensity of activation.

title: Two Possible Stories
description: Practice holding two plausible explanations for another person’s behavior before concluding what it means.
objective: Reduce mind-reading and increase curiosity about another perspective.
instructions: Describe the behavior without assigning motive.
Write two possible stories about what the person may be experiencing and one question to learn more.
prompt: What else could be true about the person’s behavior?
reflection_prompt: How did uncertainty make room for empathy?
expected_behavior: Separates observed behavior from assumptions about another person’s intent.

title: Reflect the Feeling
description: Practice acknowledging another person’s likely feeling without immediately fixing, judging, or comparing it.
objective: Communicate emotional understanding before moving to solutions.
instructions: In a conversation, use a tentative reflection such as ‘That sounds...’.
Ask whether you understood correctly and listen to the correction.
prompt: What feeling might be present beneath the person’s words?
reflection_prompt: What did acknowledgment make possible before advice?
expected_behavior: Acknowledges emotion tentatively and checks accuracy before advising.

title: Read the Room
description: Observe how context, participation, and energy shape what a group may need from you.
objective: Improve awareness of group context before acting.
instructions: After a group interaction, note who spoke, who was interrupted, energy shifts, and the stated goal.
Choose one inclusive action for the next interaction.
prompt: What did the group’s behavior communicate beyond the words?
questions: Who had less space than others?
reflection_prompt: What small change could improve participation?
expected_behavior: Adjusts participation based on group context and inclusion signals.

title: Make Space Intentionally
description: Use a simple conversational behavior to invite quieter or overlooked perspectives into a group.
objective: Practice inclusive participation without putting someone on display.
instructions: Choose a low-risk meeting or conversation.
Pause after your point, invite a perspective, and allow silence rather than answering for the person.
prompt: Whose perspective could improve this conversation if there were more room for it?
questions: How can you invite without pressuring?
reflection_prompt: What did you learn from changing the conversational space?
expected_behavior: Creates respectful opportunities for less-heard perspectives.

title: Trust Deposit
description: Choose a small reliable action that demonstrates care, competence, or respect in an important relationship.
objective: Build trust through consistent observable behavior.
instructions: Identify what the person currently needs from the relationship.
Make one specific promise you can keep and complete it within the agreed time.
prompt: What small dependable action would make trust more visible?
reflection_prompt: How did reliability affect the relationship’s ease?
expected_behavior: Builds trust through clear commitments and dependable follow-through.

title: Repair With Ownership
description: Plan a repair conversation that acknowledges impact, listens, and makes a realistic behavioral commitment.
objective: Turn relational tension into a clear repair attempt.
instructions: Write what you did, the impact it may have had, and what you will do differently.
Invite the other person’s view and do not require immediate forgiveness.
prompt: What part of this tension can you own without controlling the other person’s response?
reflection_prompt: What would ongoing repair look like beyond one conversation?
expected_behavior: Takes specific ownership and follows repair language with changed behavior.

title: Emotion and Outcome Review
description: Review an emotionally important interaction to connect internal state, behavior, impact, and learning.
objective: Integrate emotional data into future behavior choices.
instructions: Record your state before, during, and after the interaction.
Name the behavior that helped, the behavior that hurt, and one alternative response.
prompt: What did your emotional state make easier or harder in this interaction?
reflection_prompt: What is your next opportunity to practice the alternative?
expected_behavior: Uses emotional interaction reviews to choose specific future responses.

title: Reach Out With Presence
description: Initiate a genuine contact that gives another person attention rather than asking for an immediate outcome.
objective: Strengthen connection through intentional, low-pressure contact.
instructions: Choose someone you value and send a specific note about something you appreciate or remember.
Do not attach an obligation; let the contact stand on its own.
prompt: Who would benefit from knowing that you thought of them today?
questions: What detail makes the message genuine?
reflection_prompt: What did you notice about reaching out without an agenda?
expected_behavior: Initiates genuine contact consistently and without transactional pressure.

title: Shared Attention Ritual
description: Create a short recurring moment of undivided attention with someone important to you.
objective: Make connection a visible practice rather than an occasional intention.
instructions: Choose a realistic weekly time and a simple shared activity.
Agree to remove phones or competing tasks for the first fifteen minutes.
prompt: What repeatable ritual would help this relationship feel attended to?
questions: What makes the ritual easy to keep?
reflection_prompt: How did predictable attention change the quality of contact?
expected_behavior: Protects recurring time for attentive relationship contact.

title: Capacity Check
description: Notice where an automatic yes exceeds your actual time, energy, or emotional capacity.
objective: Identify boundary needs before resentment or depletion grows.
instructions: List recent commitments and rate capacity cost from 1 to 5.
Circle one commitment that needs renegotiation, clarification, or a future limit.
prompt: Where is your yes currently costing more than you intended?
reflection_prompt: What would an honest commitment look like here?
expected_behavior: Checks capacity before agreeing and renegotiates unsustainable commitments.

title: Kind No Practice
description: Rehearse a brief refusal that is honest, respectful, and free from unnecessary justification.
objective: Communicate a limit while preserving respect and choice.
instructions: Write: I cannot [specific request]. I can [alternative] or [next availability].
Practice saying it once without adding a long apology or debate.
prompt: What do you need to decline so that your genuine commitments remain possible?
reflection_prompt: What discomfort can you allow without abandoning the limit?
expected_behavior: Communicates limits directly and follows through without overexplaining.

title: Give and Receive Balance
description: Review the flow of support in a relationship and identify one healthy way to rebalance it.
objective: Notice whether support is mutual, avoid scorekeeping, and clarify needs.
instructions: Map what you give, receive, request, and avoid requesting.
Choose one small action that makes reciprocity more honest.
prompt: Where could this relationship benefit from a clearer exchange of support?
questions: What do you struggle to receive?
reflection_prompt: What does mutuality mean here beyond keeping a score?
expected_behavior: Communicates support needs and participates in reciprocal relationships.

title: Ask for Specific Help
description: Turn a vague wish for support into a clear request that gives another person a realistic choice.
objective: Make help-seeking easier for both people.
instructions: Name the situation, the kind of help, and the time or effort involved.
Ask one person and accept their answer without making it a test of care.
prompt: What support would genuinely help, and who is reasonably positioned to offer it?
reflection_prompt: How did specificity affect your willingness to ask?
expected_behavior: Makes specific support requests and respects the other person’s capacity.

title: Needs Beneath Positions
description: Map the underlying needs behind two opposing requests to find a wider set of possible solutions.
objective: Move a conflict from fixed positions toward shared needs.
instructions: Write each person’s stated position without caricature.
For each, ask what need, fear, or value the position may protect.
prompt: What does each person need that the stated position is trying to secure?
reflection_prompt: What third option becomes visible when needs are named?
expected_behavior: Explores needs and shared interests before proposing conflict solutions.

title: Repair Dialogue Rehearsal
description: Rehearse a short dialogue that names impact, listens to the other view, and proposes a next step.
objective: Prepare for direct conflict repair without rehearsing blame.
instructions: Write your opening in two sentences: impact and intention.
Write three possible responses from the other person and a curious reply to each.
prompt: How can you begin this conversation in a way that makes truth safer to hear?
questions: What outcome is within your control?
reflection_prompt: Which line keeps you open without abandoning your experience?
expected_behavior: Enters conflict repair with clear impact language and listening readiness.

title: Specific Appreciation
description: Offer appreciation that names a person’s observable contribution and its meaningful effect.
objective: Strengthen relationships through precise appreciation.
instructions: Choose one person and identify a specific behavior from the past week.
Tell them what you noticed and why it mattered to you or others.
prompt: What contribution deserves to be seen rather than assumed?
reflection_prompt: How did precise gratitude differ from a general compliment?
expected_behavior: Expresses timely, specific appreciation to strengthen connection.

title: Relationship Weather Map
description: Review important relationships for warmth, strain, reciprocity, and the next respectful action.
objective: Choose relationship maintenance actions intentionally.
instructions: List five relationships and rate connection, trust, and current strain from 1 to 5.
Choose one relationship and one action that fits its actual need.
prompt: Which relationship needs attention, appreciation, space, or repair?
questions: What action would be welcome rather than intrusive?
reflection_prompt: What did the map help you notice before the next crisis?
expected_behavior: Maintains relationships through timely actions matched to relational context.

title: Energy Signal Log
description: Track activities that increase or drain energy to gather evidence about interests and work values.
objective: Identify recurring interest signals from lived experience.
instructions: For three recent activities, record energy before, during, and after.
Note the part that engaged you and the value it expressed.
prompt: Which activities leave you more curious, capable, or alive afterward?
questions: What feature of the activity mattered?
reflection_prompt: What career hypothesis could this evidence support?
expected_behavior: Uses repeated experience to form more grounded career hypotheses.

title: Work Values Trade-Off
description: Explore what you prioritize when desirable work conditions cannot all be maximized at once.
objective: Make work-value priorities explicit for future choices.
instructions: Rank autonomy, learning, stability, impact, income, belonging, flexibility, and recognition.
Choose two trade-offs and describe the conditions under which each would be acceptable.
prompt: When work options conflict, what are you unwilling to lose?
questions: Which value is a preference versus a need?
reflection_prompt: How will this ranking change your next career conversation?
expected_behavior: Evaluates career options against explicit personal work values.

title: Transferable Skill Inventory
description: Translate recent work, study, volunteer, or life experiences into capabilities with observable evidence.
objective: Build a practical inventory of transferable skills.
instructions: List five recent responsibilities and the actions they required.
Name the transferable skill and one result or artifact that demonstrates it.
prompt: What can you reliably do that a future role might value?
questions: What evidence would convince a skeptical reader?
reflection_prompt: Which skill deserves stronger practice or visibility?
expected_behavior: Describes skills with behavioral evidence rather than broad self-labels.

title: Evidence Story Builder
description: Organize one capability into a concise situation, action, result, and learning story.
objective: Prepare credible evidence for growth conversations and applications.
instructions: Choose one skill and write the situation, your action, the result, and what you learned.
Underline your contribution and remove claims that lack evidence.
prompt: What story proves this skill through what you actually did?
questions: What changed because of your action?
reflection_prompt: What part of the story needs stronger evidence?
expected_behavior: Communicates capability through specific actions, results, and learning.

title: Role Reality Check
description: Research one possible role by comparing its daily work, required skills, constraints, and entry paths.
objective: Replace an abstract job image with grounded role information.
instructions: Use two credible role descriptions and one first-person account.
Record recurring tasks, skills, trade-offs, and one question still unanswered.
prompt: What does this role actually ask someone to do on an ordinary day?
reflection_prompt: What next experiment would test your interest in the role?
expected_behavior: Explores career options using concrete role evidence and explicit uncertainties.

title: Informational Conversation Plan
description: Prepare respectful questions for someone who can describe a career path from direct experience.
objective: Learn from practitioners through focused, non-transactional questions.
instructions: Choose a person and write a brief context-setting invitation.
Prepare five questions about daily work, entry learning, trade-offs, and advice.
prompt: What could a practitioner reveal that online research cannot?
questions: What will you do with what you learn?
reflection_prompt: Which answer most changed your career hypothesis?
expected_behavior: Conducts focused learning conversations with clear intent and gratitude.

title: A Twelve-Week Direction
description: Turn a career direction into a short growth cycle with an outcome, milestones, and review dates.
objective: Create a measurable and reviewable career growth goal.
instructions: Write the desired outcome in observable terms.
Add three milestones, a weekly action, evidence of progress, and a review date.
prompt: What meaningful career progress could you demonstrate in twelve weeks?
reflection_prompt: Which milestone should begin within the next seven days?
expected_behavior: Pursues career growth through specific milestones and reviewable evidence.

title: Skill Growth Ladder
description: Break one desired capability into observable levels from beginner practice to independent performance.
objective: Design a staged plan for building a career-relevant skill.
instructions: Name the target skill and define what beginner, capable, and independent look like.
Choose one practice activity and one feedback source for each stage.
prompt: What would visible progress in this skill look like at each level?
reflection_prompt: Which next level is challenging but realistically reachable?
expected_behavior: Builds skills through staged practice, feedback, and observable criteria.

title: Career Option Scorecard
description: Compare career options against evidence, values, learning potential, constraints, and uncertainty.
objective: Make career choices transparently rather than by mood alone.
instructions: Choose five criteria and weight each from 1 to 5.
Score two options, record evidence and uncertainty, then identify what information would change the result.
prompt: What would make one direction a better fit for the life and person you are building?
questions: Which score is weakest in evidence?
reflection_prompt: What is the next low-risk test of the leading option?
expected_behavior: Compares options using explicit criteria and identifies information gaps.

title: Next-Step Implementation Plan
description: Convert a career intention into an if-then plan tied to a calendar cue and a small evidence-producing action.
objective: Make career exploration and growth action more consistent.
instructions: Choose one next step that creates information, skill, or connection.
Write: If it is [time/cue], then I will [action] for [duration], and record [evidence].
prompt: What action will turn career thinking into evidence this week?
questions: What cue and duration make it realistic?
reflection_prompt: What evidence did the action produce, and what does it suggest next?
expected_behavior: Follows career intentions with scheduled, evidence-producing actions.

title: Visible Contribution Log
description: Record small contributions that show how your actions create value for a person, team, or shared result.
objective: Build grounded confidence from recent observable contributions.
instructions: List three actions from this week that helped someone or improved an outcome.
Write the capability and result connected to each action.
prompt: What value did your actions create that deserves to be counted?
questions: What pattern appears across the contributions?
reflection_prompt: How can this evidence guide your next stretch opportunity?
expected_behavior: Recognizes and communicates personal contribution using specific evidence.

title: Audience Adaptation Check
description: Rewrite one message for a busy reader, a worried reader, and a technical reader while preserving its intent.
objective: Adapt communication to audience needs without losing the core message.
instructions: Choose a real message with a clear purpose.
Rewrite its opening and next step for three audiences, then compare what changed.
prompt: What does this audience need first in order to understand and act?
reflection_prompt: How did audience awareness improve the message?
expected_behavior: Adapts message structure and detail to the listener’s context.

title: Compassionate Boundary Read
description: Practice recognizing another person’s feelings while deciding what support you can responsibly provide.
objective: Balance empathy with clear awareness of personal limits.
instructions: Read a situation where someone asks for more support than you can give.
Write an empathic acknowledgment, a truthful limit, and one available alternative.
prompt: How can you care about the feeling without taking responsibility for fixing everything?
questions: What support is within your role and capacity?
reflection_prompt: How did the boundary protect rather than cancel empathy?
expected_behavior: Responds with empathy while maintaining appropriate personal boundaries.
